style: An intimate cinematic telling of an Akan Anansesem, grounded in oral-storytelling rhythm and dry, humane wit. Clear natural English, never childish, grandiose, theatrical, or like an advertisement. Preserve the names Kwaku Ananse and Ntikuma. Pronounce Ananse as ah-NAHN-seh and Ntikuma as en-tee-KOO-mah. Speak the recorded climbing and scattering sounds as living story sounds rather than literal English words. Leave a short natural breath after every line.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.style: A warm mature storyteller with spacious phrasing, attentive to physical comedy and the story's turn without announcing a moral.

speakers.name: Kwaku Ananse
speakers.style: Quick, proud, inventive, and certain of himself; frustration should sharpen his wit without turning him into a cartoon villain.

speakers.name: Ntikuma
speakers.style: A small, observant child speaking simply and respectfully, with no smugness and no exaggerated child voice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Long ago, Kwaku Ananse swept together every scrap of wisdom he could find on earth.
lines.direction: Open with an old-story cadence and a wide sense of the world; lightly energize swept together.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He packed it all into a gourd pot—every answer, every secret, every clever thought.
lines.direction: Draw close to the gourd; make the three final items tactile and increasingly compressed.

lines.speaker: Kwaku Ananse
lines.text: At last, all wisdom is mine. I shall hang it where no one else can reach it.
lines.direction: Quiet triumph and absolute self-satisfaction; savor mine, then make the plan sound flawless.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He tied the gourd in front of him and came to the foot of a tall tree.
lines.direction: Move from close rope work into the vertical scale of the tree; unhurried and visual.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ananse climbed. The pot struck the trunk, caught his legs, and dragged him down.
lines.direction: Use clean physical beats with a dry final drop; do not oversell the comedy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He tried again, and again. Each time, the wisdom at his belly kept him from rising.
lines.direction: Let the repetition carry effort; slow slightly on the contradiction in the final phrase.

lines.speaker: Ntikuma
lines.text: Father, why not turn the gourd around and carry it on your back? Then you can climb.
lines.direction: A sincere practical suggestion from below, respectful and obvious rather than clever or teasing.

lines.speaker: Kwaku Ananse
lines.text: Away with you and your old-fashioned sayings!
lines.direction: A quick defensive snap from wounded pride; energetic but not shouted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But after one more useless attempt, Ananse stopped. He turned the gourd behind him.
lines.direction: Land stopped in a small pocket of silence; make the turn deliberate and reluctant.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Up he went—kra, kra, kra—swiftly to the place where the branches spread.
lines.direction: Brighten and accelerate through the climbing sound, then open the final phrase into the canopy.

lines.speaker: Kwaku Ananse
lines.text: I gathered all wisdom, yet my little child has shown me what I could not see.
lines.direction: A genuine stunned realization edged with embarrassment; quieter and slower than his earlier boast.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He tore the gourd free and hurled it down. Tintini! Tesee! Wisdom scattered below, beyond Ananse’s keeping.
lines.direction: Build through the throw, give the two Akan sound words crisp musical force, then widen and soften the last sentence.
